paraphrase: One should meditate on the 'point of light' (tejobindu), subtle and beyond the senses, hard to see and reach; it is for the one who has conquered food, anger, association, the senses and the pairs of opposites.

checks.note: E-text 1.1-3 located in the e-text; the passage matches the paraphrase.

paraphrase: The limbs are fifteen: yama, niyama, tyāga, mauna, deśa, kāla, āsana, mūlabandha, dehasāmya, dṛksthiti, prāṇasaṃyamana, pratyāhāra, dhāraṇā, ātmadhyāna and samādhi.

checks.note: E-text 1.15-16 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'yamo hi niyamastyāgo maunaṃ deśaśca kālataḥ | āsanaṃ mūlabandhaścadehasāmyaṃ ca dṛksthitiḥ || 15 ||…').

paraphrase: Each limb is knowledge: yama is restraint of the senses by the knowledge 'all is Brahman'; niyama the flow of like thoughts; silence is not mere silence of speech (that is for children); the true seat is where Brahman-contemplation flows; the true root-lock is Brahman, root of the worlds; evenness of body is dissolving in the even Brahman, not the straightness of a dry tree; the true gaze is seeing the world as Brahman, not looking at the nose-tip; prāṇāyāma is stopping all modifications by seeing all as Brahman — negating the world is exhalation, 'I am Brahman' inhalation, steadiness retention.

checks.note: E-text 1.17-32 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'sarvaṃ brahmeti vai jñānādindriyagrāmasaṃyamaḥ | yamo'yamiti samprokto'bhyasanīyo muhurmuhuḥ || 17…').

paraphrase: This (inner prāṇāyāma) is for the awakened; pressing the nose is for the ignorant.

checks.note: E-text 1.33 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'tatastadvṛttinai-ścalyaṃ kumbhakaḥ prāṇasaṃyamaḥ | ayaṃ cāpi prabuddhānāmajñānāṃ ghrāṇapīḍanam || 33…').

paraphrase: In practising samādhi obstacles arise: lack of inquiry, sloth, desire for enjoyment, dissolution (laya), darkness, distraction, radiance (tejas), sweating and blankness; the knower of Brahman should avoid them.

checks.note: E-text 1.40-41 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'samādhau kriyamāṇe tu vighnā-nyāyānti vai balāt | anusandhānarāhityamālasyaṃ bhogalālasam || 40…').

paraphrase: By thinking of an existent one becomes it, by thinking of the void, void; by the thought of Brahman, fullness; those who merely talk of Brahman without that inner state, attached to pleasure, are born again and again.

checks.note: E-text 1.42-47 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'bhāvavṛttyā hi bhāvatvaṃ śūnyavṛttyā hi śūnyatā | brahma-vṛttyā hi pūrṇatvaṃ tayā pūrṇatvamabhyaset || 42 ||…').

paraphrase: Kumāra asks Śiva about the partless, single-flavoured pure consciousness; Śiva teaches that everything — self, world, teacher, scripture — is that consciousness alone.
speaker: Śiva

paraphrase: Kumāra asks about the one liberated in life and the one liberated without body: the jīvanmukta abides as pure consciousness, free of 'I' and 'mine', while the body continues; the videhamukta is Brahman without remainder.

checks.note: E-text ch. 4 opens with Kumāra asking Parameśvara about the state of the jīvanmukta and the videhamukta.

paraphrase: Nidāgha asks Ṛbhu to teach discrimination of self and not-self; Ṛbhu teaches that the Self is beyond the three states, bodies and sheaths, and all else is not-self and unreal.
